findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, making the regression test unreliable
findings.body: The new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a background thread that repeatedly calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` while the main thread deletes groups, but it never calls `Thread.join()` (or any other synchronization) on that thread before asserting `caughtExceptions` is empty. Because `deletedAll.set(true)` is set immediately after the delete loop finishes and the assertion runs right after, the reader thread may still be mid-request (or may not have started at all) when the check executes. Any exception thrown by the reader thread after the assertion point is silently lost, so the test can pass even though the concurrency bug this PR is meant to fix still exists. In addition, the thread is not guaranteed to terminate before the test method returns, leaking a running thread into subsequent tests.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() silently returns null instead of surfacing the stale-group condition
findings.body: The fix changes `getSubGroupsCount()` to return `null` when the underlying group can no longer be loaded from the delegate (e.g. because it was concurrently deleted), instead of throwing an NPE. While this avoids the crash, it changes the contract of `GroupModel#getSubGroupsCount()`, which elsewhere in the codebase (and in other GroupModel implementations) is expected to return a non-null `Long`. Callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` (`representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())`) now may propagate a `null` subgroup count into REST responses or downstream logic that may not expect `null`, potentially moving the NPE to a different, less obvious location instead of truly fixing the root cause (stale cached group reference being used after the entity was deleted).

findings.title: No direct/unit-level regression test for the fixed NPE in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount
findings.body: The only test added for this bug fix is a broad integration test with background concurrent HTTP calls and group deletion, which is inherently timing-dependent and does not deterministically exercise the exact code path that was fixed (`GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` being called after the cached group's backing entity was deleted). There is no focused test (e.g., at model/cache level) that directly triggers `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` on a GroupAdapter whose underlying group has been removed, to verify the method now returns `null` instead of throwing an NPE.
